frs_sections.title: At some later time, the master attempts to complete the exclusive operation by performing an exclusive write
frs_sections.content:
to the same address, and with an AWID that matches the ARID used for the exclusive read.

                     3.    This exclusive write access is signaled as either:
                           •      Successful, if no other master has written to that location since the exclusive read access. In this case
                                  the exclusive write updates memory.
                           •      Failed, if another master has written to that location since the exclusive read access. In this case the
                                  memory location is not updated.
                           A master might not complete the write portion of an exclusive operation. The exclusive access monitoring

frs_sections.content:
address to other caching master components that can hold a copy, on the snoop address channel. In this
                          context, these are snooped master components.

                    3.    One of the following now occurs:
                          •      If any snooped master component holds the requested cache line, it is expected to indicate this by:
                                 —      responding on the snoop response channel
                                 —     providing the data to the interconnect, on the snoop data channel.
                                 The interconnect then provides the data, with an associated response, to the initiating master
                                 component on the read data channel.

frs_sections.content:
removed, by issuing a ReadUnique transaction on the read address channel.

                    2.    The interconnect passes the transaction to other caches on the snoop address channel.

frs_sections.title: Where applicable, a snooped master component responds to the transaction using the snoop response channel
frs_sections.content:
to indicate that it has the requested cache line. It also provides the cache line to the interconnect, using the
                          snoop data channel.

frs_sections.title: The interconnect passes the cache line, together with a response, to the initiating master, using the read data
frs_sections.content:
channel.

                                   Note
                          If no copies of the cache line are found during the snoop, a read of main memory is performed. The
                          interconnect then passes the cache line and a response to the initiating master component, on the read data
                          channel.

frs_sections.title: The master component performs the store and uses the RACK signal to indicate that the transaction has
frs_sections.content:
completed.

                            Note
                    While the cache line remains unique, loads and stores can be performed with no need for transactions to be broadcast
                    to other caches.


                    Store operations for an entire cache line

                    A master component that is storing an entire cache line does not have to obtain data before storing the cache line.
                    An example sequence is:

frs_sections.title: The initiating master component requests a unique copy of the cache line by issuing a MakeUnique
frs_sections.content:
transaction on the read address channel. This removes all other copies of the cache line.

                    2.    The interconnect passes the transaction to other caches on the snoop address channel.

frs_sections.title: Snooped master components respond to the transaction using the snoop response channel to indicate that the
frs_sections.content:
cache line has been successfully removed.

                    4.    A response is provided to the initiating master component, using the read data channel.

                                   Note
                          Only the response fields are valid. No data transfer occurs.


                    5.    The master component performs the store and uses the RACK signal to indicate that the transaction has
                          completed.

frs_sections.content:
transaction on the read address channel. This removes all other copies of the cache line and writes any dirty
                      copy to main memory.

                               Note
                      This transaction does not return the cache line to the initiating master component.


                2.    The interconnect passes the transaction to other caches on the snoop address channel. Snooped master
                      components respond to the transaction using the snoop response channel to indicate:
                      •     that the cache line has been successfully removed
                      •     whether a dirty cache line must be written to main memory by the interconnect.

frs_sections.title: If a dirty cache line is being written to main memory, the appropriate snooped master provides the dirty cache
frs_sections.content:
line to the interconnect, using the snoop data channel. The interconnect then constructs the transaction to
                      write the dirty cache line back to main memory.

                4.    A response is provided to the initiating master component, using the read data channel.

                               Note
                      Only the response fields are valid. No data transfer occurs.


                5.    The master component performs the store and uses the RACK signal to indicate that the transaction has
                      completed.

                Overlapping store operations

                If two master components attempt simultaneous Shareable store operations to the same cache line, the interconnect

frs_sections.title: A coherent transaction is checked against subsequent transactions from other master components, to ensure
frs_sections.content:
correct processing order.

                     4.       The interconnect determines the snoop transactions that are required.

                     5.       Each cached master that receives a snoop transaction must provide a snoop response. Some masters might
                              provide snoop data to complete the snoop transaction.

                     6.       The interconnect determines whether a main memory access is required.

                     7.       The interconnect collates snoop responses and any required data.

                     8.       The initiating master component completes the transaction.

frs_sections.content:
C4.5.3        ReadClean
                    ReadClean is a read transaction that is used in a region of memory that is Shareable with other masters. A ReadClean
                    transaction is guaranteed not to pass responsibility for updating main memory to the initiating master.

                    Typically, a ReadClean transaction is used by a master that wants to obtain a clean copy of a cache line, for example
                    a master with a write-through cache.

                    The transaction response requirements are:
                    •      the IsShared response indicates if the cache line is shared or unique
                    •      the PassDirty response must be deasserted.

C4.10.2       Overlapping MakeUnique
                    If master2 has issued a MakeUnique transaction because it was performing a full cache line write, the following
                    occurs:

                    1.    Master2 issues a MakeUnique transaction.

frs_sections.content:

                          •     ReadUnique
                          •     CleanInvalid

                          At this point master2 must invalidate any local copy it has of the cache line. If master2 does not have a local

                    3.    When the MakeUnique completes, Master2 can perform its full cache line store.

C7.2.5          Mismatched shareability and cacheability
                    To prevent a loss of coherency, the protocol requires that all accesses to a particular memory location must use the
                    same values of AxCACHE and AxDOMAIN. This ensures that multiple agents accessing a particular memory
                    location agree exactly on the caches in which the memory location might be held.

                    If agents accessing the same or overlapping locations do not agree exactly on the caches in which the location might
                    be held, then this is defined as a software protocol error. See Protocol errors on page C1-154.

frs_sections.title: The interconnect component collects the acknowledgements and responds to the original DVM transaction
frs_sections.content:

C12.3.2        DVM Sync and DVM Complete transactions
                     1.     The originating master component issues the DVM Sync on its read address channel.

frs_sections.title: The interconnect component distributes the DVM Sync to all participating components using the appropriate
frs_sections.content:
snoop address channel.

                     3.     Each participating component acknowledges receipt of the DVM Sync using the snoop response channel.

frs_sections.title: The interconnect component collects the acknowledgements and responds to the original DVM Sync using
frs_sections.content:
the read data channel of the originating master component.

                     5.     Each participating component must issue a DVM Complete when it has completed all the necessary actions.
                            The DVM Complete is issued by each participating component, using its read address channel. A DVM
                            Complete on the read address channel must only be issued after the handshake of the associated DVM Sync
                            on the snoop address channel of the same master.

frs_sections.title: The interconnect component can respond immediately to the DVM Complete transaction using the read data
frs_sections.content: channel of the component that issued the DVM Complete.

frs_sections.title: The interconnect component observes all of the DVM Complete transactions and when it has received a
frs_sections.content:
DVM Complete from each participating component, it issues a DVM Complete, using the snoop address
                            channel of the master component that originally issued the DVM Sync.

frs_sections.title: The originating master component acknowledges the receipt of the DVM Complete using the snoop response
frs_sections.content:
channel.


C12.3.3        Multi-part DVM Operation transactions
                     Multi-part DVM messages are always sent as successive transactions and no other transaction can be interposed
                     between them. A master component issuing a multi-part DVM message must be able to issue the latter parts of the
                     message without requiring any other external actions to occur.

                     Each transaction of a multi-part DVM Message has a response, both on the snoop response and read data channels.

                     Each transaction of a multi-part DVM Message must use the same AXI ID. See AXI transaction identifiers on
                     page A5-78.

The SMMU uses the PA to issue the transaction for the requesting component.
The address is issued on the read address (AR) channel.

functional_requirements.text: All five transaction channels use the same VALID/READY two-wire handshake protocol.
Read address (AR), read data (R), write address (AW), write data (W), and write response (B) channels are independent.
Transactions with the same ID on the same channel must remain in issue order.
Transactions with different IDs may be reordered by the interconnect or slave.
INCR, FIXED, WRAP burst types are supported with implementation-defined max length per AXI version.
Exclusive access pairs are coordinated via AxLOCK=Exclusive and matching ID.
Bursts must not cross a 4KB address boundary.

error_response_conditions: Write access attempted to read-only region
Address decode failure (no slave at address) returns DECERR
Exclusive monitor lost returns OKAY (not EXOKAY) for the exclusive write

functional_requirements_ahb.text: All bus transfers are timed by the rising edge of HCLK.
HRESETn is active-LOW; it is the only active-LOW signal in AHB.
Each AHB transfer has an Address phase (one HCLK cycle unless extended) followed by a Data phase (one or more cycles).
Address phase of any transfer overlaps the data phase of the previous transfer (pipelined operation).
HREADY HIGH at rising HCLK marks transfer completion; HREADY LOW inserts wait states.
Each Subordinate drives its own HREADYOUT; multiplexor combines all HREADYOUTs into the single HREADY broadcast.
Address decoder generates one HSELx per Subordinate; Subordinate samples HSELx + address + control only when HREADY=HIGH.
Incrementing bursts must not cross a 1KB address boundary. Minimum Subordinate decode granularity is 1KB.
Subordinates must provide zero-wait OKAY for IDLE transfers and ignore the transfer.
Subordinates must provide zero-wait OKAY for BUSY transfers and ignore the transfer. BUSY may only appear mid-burst.
HWRITE=1 indicates write; HWRITE=0 read. Must remain constant throughout a burst.
HSIZE, HBURST, HWRITE, HPROT, HMASTLOCK, HNONSEC must remain constant across all beats of a burst.
All transfers in a burst must be aligned to the address boundary equal to the size of the transfer.
Wrapping bursts wrap at burst_beats * 2^HSIZE byte boundary.
ERROR response is a two-cycle response: HRESP=1+HREADY=0 then HRESP=1+HREADY=1.
Fixed-length bursts (INCR4/8/16, WRAP4/8/16) must terminate with a SEQ; BUSY may not end them.
Manager may change HTRANS during waited transfers only as IDLE->NONSEQ, BUSY->SEQ (fixed-length), or BUSY->other (undefined-length).
Manager may change the address during HREADY=LOW only once — during an IDLE transfer, or after an ERROR response.
If the Manager requires locked accesses it asserts HMASTLOCK. All transfers in a locked sequence must address the same Subordinate region. Recommended IDLE after a locked sequence.
HPROT provides protection info; HPROT_WIDTH 0/4/7 depending on Extended_Memory_Types property. Must remain constant throughout a burst.
HNONSEC (AHB5) is an address-phase signal; constant throughout a burst; 0=Secure, 1=Non-secure.
HEXCL/HMASTER/HEXOKAY (AHB5) implement the Exclusive Access mechanism via an Exclusive Access Monitor.
HWSTRB (Issue C optional) supports sparse writes; one strobe per 8 bits of HWDATA; same validity as HWDATA.

functional_requirements_apb.text: All transfers on the APB are timed by the rising edge of PCLK.
PRESETn is active-LOW; normally connected directly to system bus reset.
Every APB transfer takes at least two PCLK cycles: SETUP (one cycle) followed by ACCESS (one or more cycles, controlled by PREADY).
SETUP: PSELx=1, PENABLE=0; lasts exactly one PCLK cycle; unconditional transition to ACCESS.
ACCESS: PSELx=1, PENABLE=1; PREADY=0 keeps bus in ACCESS; PREADY=1 exits to IDLE (no follow-up) or SETUP (back-to-back transfer).
While PREADY=LOW during ACCESS, the bridge holds PADDR, PWRITE, PSELx, PENABLE, PWDATA, PSTRB, PPROT unchanged.
PREADY can take any value while PENABLE=LOW; fixed-2-cycle peripherals may tie PREADY HIGH.
Only one PSELx asserted per transfer (single-Subordinate select).
For read transfers, the master must drive all bits of PSTRB LOW.
There is one PSTRB strobe per 8 bits of write data: PSTRB[n] -> PWDATA[(8n+7):8n].
PSLVERR is only valid during the last cycle of an APB transfer, when PSEL, PENABLE, and PREADY are all HIGH.
APB peripherals are not required to support PSLVERR. Where absent, the bridge input is tied LOW.
A failing transfer might or might not have changed peripheral state; read transfers with error may return invalid data.
PPROT[2:0] (APB4) provides protection: [0] normal/privileged, [1] secure/nonsecure, [2] data/instruction; constant while PREADY=LOW.
APB is not pipelined; use it for low-bandwidth peripherals.

fields.ic_name: AMBA AXI / ACE Protocol Specification (ARM IHI 0022E)

functional_requirements_axi_baseline_inh.text: All five AXI transaction channels + three ACE snoop channels use the same VALID/READY handshake.
Single ACLK per interface; rising-edge sampled.
ARESETn active-LOW; async assert, sync deassert.
A burst must not cross a 4KB address boundary.

functional_requirements_ace_extensions.text: Every AR/AW must drive ARDOMAIN/AWDOMAIN selecting Non-shareable / Inner / Outer / System.
A System-domain memory location cannot be held in any cache.
Coherent transactions use ARSNOOP[3:0] / AWSNOOP[2:0]. Permitted encodings depend on ARBAR[0] + AxDOMAIN (Tables C3-7, C3-8).

ReadShared may return shared/unique copy; ReadClean must not return dirty; ReadNotSharedDirty forbids SharedDirty; ReadUnique invalidates others; CleanUnique cleans local+invalidates others; MakeUnique invalidates others without data.
Cache-maintenance: CleanShared (write-back + retain Shared), CleanInvalid (write-back + invalidate), MakeInvalid (invalidate without write-back).
Memory-update writes: WriteBack (dirty + invalidate locally), WriteClean (dirty + retain Clean), Evict (cache-line removal notification), WriteEvict (optional, requires AWUNIQUE).
Coherent writes for non-cached or ACE-Lite masters: WriteUnique (partial) and WriteLineUnique (full line).
AxBAR[0]=1 indicates a barrier transaction; AxBAR[1] encodes Memory vs Synchronization barrier.
Barrier transactions can have any AxDOMAIN; choice of domain selects barrier scope.
DVM messages use ARSNOOP=0b1110 (DVMComplete) and 0b1111 (DVMMessage) — TLB / branch-predictor / I-cache invalidate, virtual-address sync.
RRESP extended to [3:0]: [2]=PassDirty (dirty wrt memory), [3]=IsShared (another cache may hold copy).
RRESP[3:2] constant for all beats of a single burst.
RRESP[3:2] must be 0 for ReadNoSnoop, Barrier, DVM transactions.
BRESP extended to [2:0]: [2]=DataTransfer (for WriteUnique/WriteLineUnique pass-dirty completion).
AC channel: interconnect drives ACADDR/ACSNOOP/ACPROT/ACVALID; master drives ACREADY.
CR channel: master drives CRRESP[4:0] (DataTransfer/Error/PassDirty/IsShared/WasUnique) + CRVALID; interconnect drives CRREADY.
CD channel: master drives CDDATA/CDLAST/CDVALID; interconnect drives CDREADY. CD bus width may differ from RDATA/WDATA.
Master must wait for ACVALID+ACREADY before asserting CRVALID. Master must wait for ACVALID+ACREADY before asserting CDVALID.
RACK pulsed one ACLK after RLAST+RVALID+RREADY; WACK pulsed one ACLK after BVALID+BREADY. Single-cycle pulses.
Cache-line uses 5-state model UC/UD/SC/SD/I (Table C5-4).
Snoops that invalidate (ReadUnique/CleanInvalid/MakeInvalid) require CRRESP IsShared=0.
Dirty->Clean transition requires CRRESP PassDirty=1. Dirty->Invalid (not via MakeInvalid) requires PassDirty=1.
PassDirty=1 with DataTransfer=0 is illegal. IsShared=1 for ReadUnique/CleanInvalid/MakeInvalid is illegal.
ACE-Lite has no AC/CR/CD channels; restricted to ReadOnce/ReadNoSnoop/WriteUnique/WriteLineUnique/WriteNoSnoop/Barrier.

error_response_conditions: Inherited AXI: FIFO/buffer overrun, unsupported transfer size, write to read-only, slave timeout, disabled function.
ACE-specific: CRRESP[1] Error — snoop failure in cached master.
Illegal AxDOMAIN/AxSNOOP/AxBAR combinations — must be detected as protocol violation.

protocol_overview.snoop_protocol: Address-based on AC channel; response on CR; optional data on CD
protocol_overview.wire_count: 5 independent channels, each with VALID/READY pair
